title: The Sharp Border
premise: Mirabel Dravenmoor, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent years laundering their own identity as carefully as any cartel launders cash, is pulled back into the field when a dead whistleblower's voiceprint unlocks a server in Tallinn containing proof that the Meridian Trust—a charity that cleans dirty money for the powerful—is planning to stage a catastrophic 'accident' at the upcoming Geneva financial summit. As Mirabel races to trace the attack's funding through shell companies, they discover their polished cover story was built by the very people they're hunting, and that their mentor, Odile Vasseur, has been feeding them curated lies for a decade. The climax comes aboard a summit-bound train, where Mirabel must choose between exposing Odile's complicity—destroying the only family they've known—and letting the attack proceed to protect their own invisibility. In the end, Mirabel burns their false identity for good, testifies under their real name, and learns that justice outside the law still demands a self willing to stand behind it.
about_author: Mara Delacroix is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent eleven years tracing money through offshore structures before turning to fiction. They write from a different city each year and have never confirmed which parts of their novels are memoir.

chapters.title: The Clean Room
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In their Zurich apartment, Mirabel runs routine due diligence on Meridian Trust's accounts while mentally rehearsing their cover identity, 'Ren Ostrov.' The go-bag sits by the door, always packed. When a routine flag on a Tallinn server pings with a dead whistleblower's voiceprint, Mirabel's carefully ordered world tilts. Emotional beat: controlled dread beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The unlocked server contains Ansel Kask's final upload: ledgers linking Meridian Trust to a scheduled event code-named GLASS HARVEST, timed to the Geneva summit. Odile Vasseur, Mirabel's mentor, dismisses the find as a hoax—but her questions are too precise. Emotional beat: the first crack of doubt in a decade of loyalty.

chapters.title: Ren Ostrov, Fully Realized
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with a flashback in Odile's voice via recorded training tapes. Mirabel deploys the Ostrov identity to Tallinn, walking through Kask's last known haunts. They find Kask's sister, who reveals Ansel contacted someone inside Mirabel's own agency. Emotional beat: the uncanny thrill of wearing a lie that fits too well.

chapters.title: Glass Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: a Meridian operative named Corvin, cold and procedural, prepping the attack—a staged infrastructure failure disguised as an accident, funded through seventeen layers of clean money. His chapters reveal the target without naming it. Emotional beat: banal evil, meticulous and unhurried.

chapters.title: The Curated Decade
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Cross-referencing Kask's ledgers, Mirabel discovers their own cover identity was created by Meridian's forgers—that Odile built 'Mirabel Dravenmoor' as a可控 asset. A dead-drop message from Kask's sister confirms Odile met Ansel the week he died. Emotional beat: vertigo; the investigator realizes they are also the evidence.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Lake House
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Odile POV, split scene. Mirabel confronts Odile at her lake house; Odile admits she recruited Mirabel as a firewall, but insists she's been quietly sabotaging Meridian from inside for years. She offers proof—and a warning: Corvin is watching Mirabel. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth grinding against each other, neither winning.

chapters.title: Seventeen Layers
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Following the money through shell companies in Malta, Cyprus, and Delaware, Mirabel pinpoints GLASS HARVEST's target: the summit's secure data vault, whose destruction will be framed as an accident and bury evidence against a dozen governments. Corvin's team makes Mirabel in Tallinn; they barely escape. Emotional beat: hunted clarity—the truth has a shape now, and a deadline.

chapters.title: The Geneva Manifest
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with intercut Corvin. Mirabel learns the attack will trigger aboard the summit delegation's overnight train, where the vault's backup drives travel under diplomatic seal. Odile is on the passenger manifest—either fleeing, sabotaging, or bait. Mirabel boards with a forged credential and forty minutes of margin. Emotional beat: cold focus over rising panic.

chapters.title: Accident Weather
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Corvin POV, converging. In the train's service car, Mirabel disables the sabotage rig but finds Odile holding the dead-man's switch—she triggered the plot's final phase to force Meridian's handlers into the open, gambling Mirabel would stop it. Corvin corners them both. Emotional beat: betrayal and trust indistinguishable at knife's edge.

chapters.title: Under My Own Name
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel stops the attack, Corvin is arrested with the ledger trail intact, and Odile surrenders her evidence in exchange for testimony—naming Mirabel as her source. In a Geneva hearing room, Mirabel retires 'Ren Ostrov' forever and testifies as Mirabel Dravenmoor, real name, real record. The go-bag stays unpacked. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; visibility as the price and reward of justice.
